title: Bringing Enterprise-Class Computing to Defense and Commercial Edge Platforms

Our experience across PCIe, hybrid VPX, and OCP architectures allows us to support these requirements and help customers integrate enterprise-class computing into their platforms. As AI/ML, sensor processing, and autonomous applications continue to advance, computing architecture will play an increasingly important role in determining platform capabilities. Adapting enterprise computing technologies for demanding edge environments gives developers access to greater processing density and lower latency without losing sight of the physical constraints of their systems. This is the engineering challenge OSS works to solve every day.
body_markdown:
**By Mike Knowles, CEO**


The computing requirements for defense and commercial platforms have changed significantly. Artificial intelligence, machine learning, sensor processing, sensor fusion, and autonomous applications are demanding more processing power and lower latency than many existing embedded computing architectures can provide.


For platform developers, the challenge is increasing computing performance without exceeding the available Size, Weight, Power, and Cost (SWaP-C) constraints. Many of today's architectures were designed for a different generation of computing requirements and are reaching their limits as these workloads become more demanding.


I believe we need to take a closer look at how enterprise computing technologies can be adapted to address these challenges.


# What are the Limitations of Traditional Architectures?


Traditional 3U and 6U VPX architectures have served defense applications for years, but they were not designed for today's levels of AI/ML processing and sensor density.


In many implementations, available board space limits AI inferencing to one or two workloads per board. As processing requirements increase, adding more boards creates additional integration complexity, consumes valuable space, and introduces connectivity challenges.


Connecting multiple processing resources through Ethernet can also increase latency, which is a disadvantage for applications requiring real-time sensor processing and data fusion.


The issue is not simply adding more processing power. It is how efficiently that processing can be integrated and connected within the physical limitations of the platform.


# How to Leverage Enterprise Computing at the Edge


The enterprise computing industry has made significant investments in GPU performance, processing density, and high-speed connectivity. These advancements offer an opportunity to improve computing capabilities in defense and commercial applications.


Open-system enterprise technologies using PCIe and CXL provide high-bandwidth, low-latency connections between processors, accelerators, and other system resources. Compared with architectures relying on Ethernet connections between separate processing boards, these technologies can significantly reduce communication latency. Depending on the architecture, PCIe connectivity can provide improvements on the order of 1,000X.


Enterprise-class compute also offers greater processing density, allowing more AI inferencing and other compute-intensive workloads within comparable physical volumes.


For platform developers, this means an opportunity to increase computing performance without proportionally increasing the size or complexity of the system.


# Does System Integration Make a Difference?


Adopting a higher-performance GPU or processor alone does not solve the challenges associated with AI inferencing, sensor fusion, or signal processing. The entire computing architecture must be designed to support the required performance.


Processing, storage, connectivity, power consumption, thermal management, and mechanical integration all affect the finished system. In defense applications, these requirements are further complicated by environmental conditions such as extreme temperatures, shock, and vibration.


The available space and power are often fixed by the platform. Increasing computing capabilities requires balancing all these variables without compromising system performance or reliability.


This is where system-level engineering experience becomes important. Understanding how components work together and identifying potential bottlenecks are essential to developing a solution that performs as intended.


# What is OSS's Approach to Enterprise-Class Computing?


At One Stop Systems (OSS), we leverage advancements in enterprise computing and apply them to the requirements of defense and commercial edge applications.


Our focus is delivering high-performance computing with lower latency than traditional architectures while remaining within equal or smaller SWaP-C envelopes. This requires a holistic approach to system design, including power optimization, thermal management, and ruggedization.


We also recognize that customers have different architectural requirements. Some need to maintain compatibility with existing VPX infrastructure, while others are incorporating newer open standards. Our experience across PCIe, hybrid VPX, and OCP architectures allows us to support these requirements and help customers integrate enterprise-class computing into their platforms.


As AI/ML, sensor processing, and autonomous applications continue to advance, computing architecture will play an increasingly important role in determining platform capabilities. Adapting enterprise computing technologies for demanding edge environments gives developers access to greater processing density and lower latency without losing sight of the physical constraints of their systems.


This is the engineering challenge OSS works to solve every day.
